At the playground in Lisbon, a bigger boy grabbed the swing just as Nour reached it. Nour, five, stomped to the bench and sat with her arms crossed, kicking the sand.
Her mother, Camila, sat beside her. "Your eyebrows are all squished together. Are you feeling cross?"
Nour kicked harder. "No."
"Okay." Camila waited, watching the pigeons.

"Ah. That's annoying."
"I'm angry," Nour said, trying the word. "Very angry."
"That makes sense."

Avni, five, was building a tower. It fell. She threw a block at the wall, stamped, and sat with her arms folded, lip pushed out.
